title: Allowed IP ranges: no route serves the caller's address as the server resolves it, so the console cannot show an admin which address the lock-out check will judge before they save
body:
domain:ui#3 · os-bill · session_01Utp6CbPN5UYMnBaNJPJWfG

Filed by the `domain:ui#3` seat from the out-of-scope finding of #30313's card thread (os-dev-report 6654556555). Carrier: `domain:server`.

## Observed (measured at `870ebce3`)

- `AuthManager.resolveClientAddress` decides which address the `allowed_ip_ranges` save check and the sign-in gate judge (trustProxy included). The save check from #30203 (PR #30309) refuses a list that leaves that address out and names it in `constraint.clientAddress`.
- No route serves that resolved address before a save. The only way an admin learns it today is to be refused.
- The console already shows the refusal's sentence under the field on main (Playwright shot in #30313's report: `/api/settings/auth` 400 `SETTINGS_VALIDATION`, `constraint.clientAddress=127.0.0.1`, red text under the field).

## Wanted

- An authenticated read serves the caller's address exactly as `resolveClientAddress` resolves it (for example a field on an existing settings or auth read; the shape is the server lane's call). It must be the same function the save check uses, so the shown address and the judged address cannot drift.
- Then #30313 item 1 (ui) shows it beside the Allowed IP ranges field. ⛔ The client must not guess its own address.

## Not in scope

- IPv6 CIDR matching: #30320.

Blocks: #30313 (item 1).
Dedupe words: allowed ip ranges current address, resolveClientAddress read, caller client address.
